title: The Tailor’s Tale: The Lame Young Man from Baghdad and the Barber

paragraphs.en: The king of the age was told by a tailor that an extraordinary event occurred yesterday. Invited to an early morning banquet with about twenty companions, they stood in salute when a handsome stranger entered. This young man, though beautiful, was lame.
paragraphs.zh: 国王听说一位裁缝说昨天发生了一件不同寻常的事情。他被邀请参加一个清晨的宴会，大约有二十位同伴一同前往。当一位英俊的陌生人走进来时，他们纷纷起立致敬。尽管这位年轻人相貌出众，却腿脚不便。

paragraphs.en: Seeing a barber among them, he refused to sit and tried to leave. The host stopped him, asking why he would enter and then depart so quickly. The young man replied that the old barber was ill-omened, ill-behaved, bungling, shameful, and pernicious.
paragraphs.zh: 见到一位理发师在场，他不肯坐下，试图离开。主人阻止了他，问他为何刚进来就要走。年轻人回答说，那位老理发师不吉利、行为不当、技术拙劣、丢人现眼且有害无益。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused as morning approached, but Dinarzad urged her to continue. Shahrazad promised an even more entertaining story if she lived another night.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹正要暂停讲述，但迪纳兹德催促她继续。莎赫拉兹答应如果再活一夜，一定会讲一个更加引人入胜的故事。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad recounted:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙赫拉兹如此讲述：

paragraphs.en: In Baghdad, the tailor had a misfortune with a barber that led to his lameness and departure from the city. He swore never to be in the same place or city as this barber again. Now finding him at their banquet, he vowed to leave immediately unless he shared his story.
paragraphs.zh: 在巴格达，裁缝与一位理发师发生了不幸的事，导致他瘸了腿并离开了这座城市。他发誓再也不会出现在同一个地方或同一个城市中见到这位理发师。如今，在宴会上遇到对方，他当即表示除非理发师愿意分享他的故事，否则自己将立即离开。

paragraphs.en: The companions urged him to sit and tell what happened between them in Baghdad. The young man agreed, though the barber turned pale and bowed his head.
paragraphs.zh: 同伴们催促他坐下，讲述他们在巴格达的经历。年轻人答应了，不过理发师面色苍白，低下了头。

paragraphs.en: My father, one of Baghdad's wealthiest men, left me his fortune when he died. Afterward, I began living lavishly and avoiding women due to my hatred for them. One day, while walking in the city, a group of women blocked my path, forcing me into an alley where I sat until evening.
paragraphs.zh: 我的父亲是巴格达最富有的人之一，在他去世时将他的财产留给了我。此后，我开始过着奢侈的生活，并且因为厌恶女性而避开她们。有一天，我在城里散步时，一群妇女挡住了我的去路，把我逼进了一条小巷里，直到傍晚我才坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: There, a young lady appeared at a window, tending flowers, her beauty overwhelming. She smiled, changing my feelings from hate to love.
paragraphs.zh: 在那里，一位年轻女子出现在窗前，手中拿着花，美貌惊人。她微微一笑，让我从仇恨中转变为了爱意。

paragraphs.en: The judge of Baghdad rode by later that day, leading me to believe he was the woman's father. Heartbroken, I returned home and lay in bed, consumed with passion. My relatives noticed my distress but could not console me for several days.
paragraphs.zh: 当天晚些时候，巴格达的法官骑马经过，这让我以为他是那位女子的父亲。心碎之下，我回到家中躺在床上，满脑子都是她。几天里，亲戚们虽然注意到了我的愁苦，却也无法安慰我。

paragraphs.en: One evening, an old woman visited and guessed my problem immediately. She comforted me, saying, "Son, be cheerful; tell me what ails you, and I will help." Her words eased my heart, and we talked until morning came.
paragraphs.zh: 一个傍晚，一位老妇人来访，立刻猜到了我的烦恼。她安慰我说：“儿子，别愁眉苦脸；告诉我出了什么问题，我会帮你解决的。”她的话让我心情舒畅，我们一直聊到天亮。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued her tale: The tailor told the king of China that the young man had spoken to his guests about his feelings. An old woman then recited verses expressing his confusion and pain, comparing the lady's beauty to a radiant brow and cheeks but her actions to those of a cruel mistress who set his heart on fire.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹继续讲述她的故事：裁缝向中国国王透露，那个年轻人曾与他的客人谈论过自己的感受。随后，一位老妇人吟诵了几行诗句，表达了年轻人的困惑和痛苦。她将那位女士的美貌比作光彩照人的眉毛和脸颊，但她的行为却如同一个残忍的情妇，让年轻人心如火烧。

paragraphs.en: Cheeks in dust and eyes with tears, Mourning lost love and days of yore. Helpless I grieve, yet what use sighs? Without her, dead though not in grave.
paragraphs.zh: 满脸尘土，双目含泪， 哀悼往昔的爱与逝去的日子。 我无力悲泣，可叹息又有何用？ 没有她，虽未长眠地下，却已如死。

paragraphs.en: Haunted by memories, face serene, Neither joy nor rage, but love's refrain.
paragraphs.zh: 萦绕着往昔的记忆，面容平静， 既非喜悦也非愤怒，唯有爱的低吟。

paragraphs.en: Heart, break with grief; let soul expire. O heart in silver cage, despair! Consumed with love, impatient still, Watch rivals press, reproach them ill.
paragraphs.zh: 心啊，因悲伤而碎裂；让灵魂消逝吧。银笼中的心啊，绝望吧！纵然痴情已深，依然焦躁难耐，眼见对手逼近，只能怨恨责备。

paragraphs.en: O will the good old days return? How can I forget her form and mien?
paragraphs.zh: 啊，那些美好的旧时光何时能再现？我怎么可能会忘记她的模样呢？

paragraphs.en: In embrace, her body lit by sun, Dark delight on green grass soft as down. Fondling cheeks like silk, clutching gold, Softness like flowers or a heart unshown.
paragraphs.zh: 在拥抱中，她的身体沐浴在阳光下，在柔软如绒的绿草上散发出深邃的愉悦。轻抚着丝绸般细腻的脸颊，紧握着金色的柔情，如同花朵或未展的心灵一般温柔。

paragraphs.en: Let watchman come; she's saved my hours! My love is constant, never swerves. Unlike the others, I have loved and will, Keeping honor, not in vain, but well.
paragraphs.zh: 让守夜人来吧，她救了我的时光！我的爱是坚定的，从不改变。与他人不同的是，我真心相爱，并将永远如此，坚守荣誉，绝非徒劳无功，而是值得的。

paragraphs.en: In bliss we lived until our Eden fell. Now all has vanished, days of yore. Alas for those with black-eyed deer!
paragraphs.zh: 我们在天堂般的幸福中生活，直到我们的伊甸园不复存在。如今，往日的一切都已烟消云散！唉，那些长着黑眼睛的鹿啊！

paragraphs.en: If they return, eternal fasting I'll swear, For without her, outcast, love's victim I'll be. Morning came; Shahrazad was silent then. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a tale!"
paragraphs.zh: 如果他们回来，我发誓将终生禁食。没有她，我将成为被遗弃的爱的牺牲品。天亮了；沙赫拉兹德这时沉默不语。丁纳扎德说道：“ sister，你讲了个怎样的故事啊！”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad replied, "More tomorrow night!"
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹回答说：“明天晚上再讲吧！”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began: O happy King, the tailor spoke to China’s king, Of a young man who told guests of his love's decline.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙海拉卓开口说道：“幸福的国王啊，裁缝向中国的国王讲述了一个年轻人的故事，他向客人诉说了恋人渐行渐远的心境。”

paragraphs.en: The old woman said to me, "Son, tell me your story." After I shared it, she replied, "That young lady is the daughter of Baghdad's judge, kept in strict seclusion. The place where you saw her is her private room.
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人对我说：“儿子，把你的故事告诉我。”听完后，她回答道：“那个年轻女子是巴格达法官的女儿，一直被严格地幽禁着。你见到她的地方正是她的私人房间。”

paragraphs.en: Her parents live below in the great hall. I often visit her and will help you through me. Gird your loins."
paragraphs.zh: 她的父母住在下面的大厅里。我经常去看她，我会帮你跟她沟通。束紧你的腰带。

paragraphs.en: When the old woman returned the next morning, crestfallen, she said, "Son, don't ask how I fared with the young lady. She warned me to stop talking about you or face punishment." Despite this, she vowed to try again.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，老妇人垂头丧气地回来后说：“儿子，别问我与那位小姐的谈话怎么样。她警告我要是再提你，就会遭到惩罚。”尽管如此，她还是发誓要再试一次。

paragraphs.en: Hearing her words, I felt worse and repeated, "Alas, how cruel is love!" The old woman visited daily as my illness dragged on, causing despair among physicians, sages, and my family.
paragraphs.zh: 听到她的话，我更加忧心忡忡，不禁脱口而出：“唉，爱情多么残酷！”那位老妇人每日前来探望，我的病情久治不愈，令医生、智者和家人感到绝望。

paragraphs.en: One day, the old woman whispered to me, "You must give me a reward for good news." Sitting at my head, she continued, "Yesterday, I went to see her. She welcomed me and noticed my distress.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，老妇人轻声对我说：“你必须给我点报酬，好让我把好消息带给她。”她坐在我的枕边，继续说道：“昨天我去探望了她。她热情地接待了我，并注意到了我的愁容。”

paragraphs.en: When asked what was wrong, I told her about your condition and how you saw her by the window, falling in love with her."
paragraphs.zh: 当被问及出了什么问题时，我告诉她你的状况，以及你透过窗户看见她，并因此坠入爱河的事情。

paragraphs.en: She added, "These were his verses: By the rare treasure of your lovely face, don't kill your lover with your cruel disdain. His heart is intoxicated with love, his wasting body racked and torn with pain."
paragraphs.zh: 她接着说：“这是他的诗：凭你那可爱的容颜，不要用残酷的冷漠杀死你的爱人。他心醉于爱恋，身体因相思而憔悴不堪。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued her tale to the king:
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹继续向国王讲述她的故事：

paragraphs.en: The tailor recounted that the young man from Baghdad told his guests about a visit. The old woman said he fared poorly with the lady and returned home worse than before. She feared he might die and suggested he come on Friday, before noon prayer, so she could meet him secretly in her room.
paragraphs.zh: 裁缝讲述说，来自巴格达的年轻人曾向客人们提起一次访问。老妇人说他与那位女士的会面并不顺利，回来时比之前更糟糕。她担心他会因此病倒，建议他在星期五中午祈祷前前来，好在她的房间里秘密相见。

paragraphs.en: Hearing this, Shahrazad's distress lifted. The old woman sat beside her and instructed to be ready for Friday. After receiving payment, she left, leaving the young man feeling hopeful and recovered by his family's joy.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这里，沙赫拉扎德的忧虑也随之消散。老妇人坐在她身旁，嘱咐她准备好迎接周五的到来。拿到酬金后，老妇人起身离开了。留下那个年轻人感到充满希望，并被家人的喜悦所治愈。

paragraphs.en: The king, intrigued, vowed not to kill Shahrazad until he heard more of the hunchback’s story.
paragraphs.zh: 国王对此颇感兴趣，誓言在听完全残青年的故事之前不会杀掉沙海拉罕。

paragraphs.en: On Friday, I recovered enough to visit the bath and wash away my illness. However, I preferred a haircut over bathing. I asked for a barber who was sensible and quiet.
paragraphs.zh: 星期五，我恢复了一些，便去浴室洗了个澡，试图洗净病痛的痕迹。不过，我还是更倾向于理个发。于是，我请来了一个稳重又安静的理发师。

paragraphs.en: The servant brought in an old barber who began to inquire about my health. He suggested bloodletting or shaving, but I insisted on just a haircut to avoid his chatter.
paragraphs.zh: 仆人带来了一位老剃头师傅，他开始询问我的身体状况。他建议我放血或者刮痧，但我坚持只要剪个头发，以免听他的啰嗦。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused her tale as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked, "What a fascinating story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; there's much more to come if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹讲到此处，晨光已渐渐临近。丁纳扎德不禁赞叹：“真是引人入胜的故事！”莎赫拉兹 aden：“还得等到明天晚上，如果国王饶恕我的话，还有更多精彩等着你呢。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that the tailor told the king of China about the young man’s conversation with his guests.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，裁缝向中国的国王讲述了那个年轻人和他的客人们交谈的事情。

paragraphs.en: I told the barber, "I am still weak from my illness." He then produced an astrolabe from his leather bag, examined it under the sun, and declared, "Eight degrees and six minutes have passed today, a Friday in Safar 653 of the Hijra and 7320 of the Alexander era. Mars is currently ascendant, favorable for cutting hair.
paragraphs.zh: 我对理发师说：“我还在病后感到虚弱。”他随后从皮袋中取出一个天文学仪，拿阳光照了照，然后宣布：“今天是星期五，萨法尔月653年哈吉里历，亚历山大纪元7320年。火星目前当空，适合理发。”

paragraphs.en: However, you are meant to meet another person, which is ill-advised."
paragraphs.zh: 然而，你本不该遇到另一个人，这可不是个好主意。

paragraphs.en: I retorted, "Stop with your astrological nonsense! I brought you here to shave my head, not to read the stars. Get on with it or find someone else."
paragraphs.zh: 我反驳道：“住口，你的占星术鬼话不用说了！我叫你来剃头，可不是来看星相的。快点动手，不然另请高明。”

paragraphs.en: He replied, "By God, lord, even if you had asked for a simpler task, this would still be more than enough. You have a barber who is also an astrologer and physician, skilled in alchemy, grammar, lexicography, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, algebra, history, and the traditions of the Prophet."
paragraphs.zh: 他回答说：“天哪，大人，即便您要我完成一个更简单的任务，这也已经足够了。您的理发师兼占星家和医生，同时还精通炼金术、语法、词源学、逻辑学、修辞学、算术、代数学、历史以及先知的教诲。”

paragraphs.en: Shaken by his words, I said, "You will surely drive me mad today."
paragraphs.zh: 被他的话惊到，我说：“你今天肯定会把我逼疯的。”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad then remarked, "What a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad responded, "Wait until tomorrow night when I have more to tell you if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳札德不禁感叹道：“这真是个奇特而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹回答说：“等国王今晚赦免了我，我会给你讲更多。”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad spoke to the king:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙赫拉兹阿德对国王说道：

paragraphs.en: She said, "I heard that the tailor told the king about a young man who addressed his guests. The barber then added, 'Am I not known as the Silent One due to my taciturnity? My brothers are named al-Baqbuq, al-Haddar, al-Buqaybiq, al-Kuz al-Aswani, and al-Nashshar, while I am called al-Samit.
paragraphs.zh: 她说：“我听说裁缝向国王提到有个年轻人在宴会上致辞。理发师接着说：‘难道你们不知道我被称为沉默者吗？我的兄弟分别叫阿卜·巴布乌格、阿卜·哈达尔、阿卜·布卡伊比格、阿卜·库兹·阿斯瓦尼和阿卜·纳什夏尔，而我则被称为阿卜·萨米特。’”

paragraphs.en: Despite my silence, I continued speaking until the young man became frustrated and ordered his servant to give me four dinars and send me away."
paragraphs.zh: 尽管我一言不发，他还是不停地说话，直到那年轻人感到烦躁，命令仆人给我四迪纳尔，并把我打发走。

paragraphs.en: The barber responded, "O my lord, what kind of talk is this? By God, I must serve you as it is my duty to help and fulfill your need, regardless of payment. If you do not know my worth, I know yours and the esteem in which you are held because of your father."
paragraphs.zh: 理发师回答说：“我的老爷，您这是在说什么呢？天哪，我必须像尽我帮助和满足您的需求之责一样为您效劳，无论是否有报酬。如果您不了解我的价值，那我却了解您的身份以及您因父亲而受到的尊敬。”

paragraphs.en: He then recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他接着吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: I came one day to let blood for my lord, But found the season unsuitable. Instead, I spoke of many prodigies, And shared my store of knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 我有一天来为老爷放血，但发现时机不合适。于是，我谈到了许多奇闻异事，并分享了我的知识渊博。

paragraphs.en: Pleased with my talk, he said: "You are beyond compare, O mine of lore!"
paragraphs.zh: 他满意地说道：“你无与伦比，你是知识的宝库啊！”

paragraphs.en: The barber replied: "O lord of men, you are the source Of wisdom from your boundless store. O lord of grace and all munificence, O treasure house of knowledge, wit, and sense!"
paragraphs.zh: 理发师回答道：“哦，人间的主宰，您是无尽智慧的源泉。哦，恩典与慷慨的君王，知识、机智和理智的宝库！”

paragraphs.en: The tailor recounted how he recited verses to the young man from Baghdad. The father, pleased, instructed his servant to give the tailor 103 dinars and a robe of honor for his astrological observation, conversation, bloodletting, and praise. The tailor questioned the sum, but the father explained each dinar's purpose.
paragraphs.zh: 裁缝讲述了他为那位来自巴格达的年轻人诵读诗篇的情景。父亲听后非常满意，吩咐仆人给裁缝103第纳尔和一件荣誉袍子作为对他占星观测、交谈、放血以及赞美所作的报酬。裁缝对这个数目有些疑问，但父亲一一解释了每第纳尔的具体用途。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked on the story’s strangeness, to which Shahrazad replied that it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if alive.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹停下了讲述，晨光渐渐临近。丁纳札德对这个故事感到有些奇怪，莎赫拉兹回应说，这比起她第二天晚上还会讲的故事来简直不算什么。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began by saying she had heard a tailor tell the king of China about a young man from Baghdad who spoke to guests. The tailor then addressed his barber, warning him to stop talking as he was running late. The barber laughed and said that the tailor seemed foolish, unlike usual.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，莎赫拉兹朵开始说道，她听一个裁缝讲过一个来自巴格达的年轻人的故事，这个年轻人会与客人交谈。随后，裁缝转向理发师，警告他别再说话了，因为他快迟到了。理发师笑了笑，说裁缝今天的表现似乎有些傻气，与往常不同。

paragraphs.en: He quoted a poet: "Comfort the poor with money if you can, for God's recompense will be yours by right." He added that want is hard to cure but money can improve one’s condition. He advised meeting friends in peace and showing respect to parents.
paragraphs.zh: 他引用了一位诗人的诗句：“如果可以，用金钱抚慰穷人吧，因为上帝会公正地给予你回报。”他又补充说，贫困难以治愈，但金钱却能改善一个人的境况。他建议在和平中与朋友相聚，并尊重父母。

paragraphs.en: The barber concluded by saying that the tailor was excused but worried about him. He reminded the tailor that his father and grandfather always consulted him, citing proverbs: "He who takes counsel shall not be disappointed," and "He who has no mentor will never be a mentor." The barber quoted another poet: "Before you proceed to do anything, consult a mature man ere venturing."
paragraphs.zh: 理发师总结道，裁缝虽获准离开，但他仍为裁缝的处境感到担忧。他提醒裁缝，他的父亲和祖父总是向他咨询意见，并引用了一句谚语：“谋事在人，成事在天。”他还提到了另一位诗人的诗句：“凡事未做之前，先请教一位老练之人。”

paragraphs.en: Indeed, I am more experienced than you and ready to serve. You have spoken too much; all I want is a shave. He replied that he was not annoyed with me but knew my lord was displeased.
paragraphs.zh: 确实，我比你更有经验，也准备好为你服务。你话说得太多，我只想刮个胡子。他回答说，并不生气于我，只是知道我的主人有些不满。

paragraphs.en: My appointment is near; please shave quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 我的理发时间快到了，请你赶快给我剃个头。

paragraphs.en: He took the razor, sharpened it, and shaved a few hairs before holding back. "Haste is of the devil," he said, quoting a poet. "Be careful and restrain your hasty wish; be merciful to all."
paragraphs.zh: 他拿起剃刀，磨锋利了一些，刚刮了几根胡子便停了下来。“心急如焚乃魔鬼所为，”他引用了一句诗，“谨慎行事，克制你的急躁；对所有人都要仁慈。”

paragraphs.en: He then spoke of his worth, knowledge, and wisdom but was told to stop meddling.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后谈起了自己的价值、知识和智慧，但被要求不要多管闲事。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, yes, yes!" I replied, urging him not to rush. "Don’t be in a hurry; haste leads to regret," he said, adding that he feared for my well-being.
paragraphs.zh: “好，好，好！”我回答道，催促他不要急。“别着急，心急吃不了热豆腐。”他说，并补充说担心我的安危。

paragraphs.en: With three hours left before prayer, he insisted on knowing the exact time, as his merit was known and he could not base statements on conjecture.
paragraphs.zh: 距离祈祷还有三个小时，他坚持要知道确切的时间，因为他的功绩众所周知，不能凭空猜测。

paragraphs.en: He then threw down the razor and left.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后扔下剃刀，转身离去。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied that it paled in comparison to what she would tell the next night if the king spared her life.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳扎德remarked道：“这真是个奇特而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹回应说，与她若能保住性命，第二天晚上将要讲述的故事相比，这个故事简直黯然失色。

paragraphs.en: The barber put down his razor and left with an astrolabe. He returned, counting on his fingers, declaring that three hours remained until prayer time. I pleaded, "For God's sake, stop talking; you've already bothered me enough."
paragraphs.zh: 理发师放下剃刀，拿着一个天文学仪器离开了。他回来后，边数手指边宣布还有三个小时才到祈祷时间。我央求道：“求求你了，别再说话；你已经烦我够久了。”

paragraphs.en: He took out the razor again, shaved a few hairs, and said, "I don't understand your hurry, but it concerns me. Your father and grandfather would have consulted me before acting."
paragraphs.zh: 他又拿出了剃刀，刮掉了几根毛发，说道：“我不明白你为什么这么急着行动，但这让我有些担心。你父亲和祖父在行事之前肯定会咨询我的意见。”

paragraphs.en: Realizing he wouldn't leave, I thought, "It’s nearly noon, and I need to see the young lady before people return from prayer." I told him, "Be quick; I must go to a party at my friend's house." Hearing this, he said, "This is a lucky day for me.
paragraphs.zh: 意识到他不会轻易离开，我心想：“都快中午了，得赶紧去看望那位小姐，免得人们从祈祷回来找不到我。”我对他说：“你快点吧，我要去朋友家参加聚会。”听到这话，他脱口而出：“今天对我真是个好日子。”

paragraphs.en: You reminded me that yesterday I invited friends but forgot to provide food."
paragraphs.zh: 你提醒我说，我昨天请了客人却没有准备食物。

paragraphs.en: I assured him, "Don't worry; all the food and drink from my house will be yours if you hurry and shave my head." He asked, "What are you giving me?" I replied, "Five dishes, ten fried chickens, and a roasted lamb."
paragraphs.zh: 我向他保证：“别担心，如果你赶快给我剃头，我家里的所有食物和饮料你都可以享用。我给你五道菜、十只炸鸡和一只烤羊。”他问道：“你到底给了我什么？”我回答说：“就是这五道菜、十只炸鸡和一只烤羊。”

paragraphs.en: He said, "Show them to me," so I sent a servant to buy everything quickly. The barber saw the food but complained there was no wine.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“把这些都拿给我看看。”于是我派了一个仆人赶紧把东西买回来。理发师见到了食物，但抱怨说没有酒。

paragraphs.en: I brought out two flagons of wine, which he accepted with gratitude. Finally, he noted, "We have the food and wine, but we still need perfume and incense."
paragraphs.zh: 我端上了两壶酒，他感激地接过。最后，他说道：“有了食物和酒水，但我们还需要香水和香料。”

paragraphs.en: I brought him a box containing five dinars' worth of aloewood, ambergris, and musk. As time was running out, I urged, "For God's sake, take the whole box and finish shaving my head." He replied, "By God, I will not take it until I see the contents one by one."
paragraphs.zh: 我给他拿来一个装有五迪纳尔的沉香、琥珀和麝香的盒子。时间紧迫，我催促道：“求求你了，把整个盒子都拿走，给我剃完头吧。”他回答说：“天哪，我不会拿走，直到我把每一样东西都看过才行。”

paragraphs.en: The servant opened the box, and the barber threw down his astrolabe, sat down, and began to examine each item before accepting them. Meanwhile, I waited, most of my head still unshaven, until I choked with exasperation.
paragraphs.zh: 仆人打开盒子，理发师放下他的星盘，坐了下来，逐一检查每一样东西才收下。我则在一旁等待，大半边头还未刮完，终于忍无可忍地哼了一声。

paragraphs.en: Taking the razor, he came up to me and shaved a little hair, reciting:
paragraphs.zh: 拿着剃刀，他走到我跟前刮了点胡子，边做边念叨着：

paragraphs.en: "The growing boy follows his father's suit, Just as the tree grows firmly from its root."
paragraphs.zh: “这个渐渐长大的少年跟着父亲的脚步前行，正如树木牢固地从根部生长。”

paragraphs.en: He then added, "By God, my lord, I don't know whether to thank you or your father. Your generosity has made our party possible. May God preserve it and you.
paragraphs.zh: 他接着说道：“天哪，我的老爷，我不知道该感谢您还是您的父亲。您的慷慨让我们此行成为可能。愿上帝保佑您和此行顺利。”

paragraphs.en: None of my friends is worthy of it; yet they are all decent men—Zentut the bathkeeper, Sali’ the corn dealer, Sallut the beanseller, Akrasha the grocer, Sa’id the cameldriver, Suwaid the porter, Hamid the garbageman, Abu-Makarish the bath attendant, Qusaim the watchman, and Karim the groom. Each has his own dance and verses, but their best quality is that they are like your servant; they neither meddle nor talk too much."
paragraphs.zh: 我的朋友们都不配拥有它，但他们个个都是不错的家伙——比如浴池管理员詹图特、谷物商萨利、豆贩子萨卢特、杂货商阿克拉斯、骆驼夫赛义德、搬运工苏瓦伊德、垃圾清理工哈米德、浴室侍者阿布-马卡里斯、看门人库塞以及马夫卡里姆。他们各有自己的舞步和诗句，但他们的最大优点是像我的仆人一样——既不过分干涉也不多嘴多舌。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said to her sister, "What a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me!"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，沙赫札德默不作声。丁纳扎德对她说：“真是个奇异而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫札德回答道：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等明晚吧！”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard that the tailor told the king of China that the young man said to the guests: The barber praised the corn dealer, saying he sings better than the nightingale and dances with such grace that it makes men laugh until their hearts burst. He also spoke highly of the garbageman, who dances to the tambourine and even charms birds with his song, "News from my neighbor is locked in a chest."
paragraphs.zh: 我听说裁缝对中国的国王说，那个年轻人对客人说道：理发师称赞粮商说他唱得比夜莺还要动听，舞姿优雅到让人笑得几乎心碎。他还高度评价了垃圾工，后者跳舞时敲打着手鼓，甚至用他的歌“邻居的消息藏在箱子里”来吸引鸟儿的注意。

paragraphs.en: The tailor's heart raced at the sight of the lame young man from Baghdad. Fate had brought them together one night, and the tailor confessed his feelings. The young man replied with a playful retort, comparing him to a scavenger who could light a pyre.
paragraphs.zh: 看见那个来自巴格达的残疾青年，裁缝的心狂跳不已。命运让他们在一个夜晚相遇，裁缝忍不住倾诉了自己的心意。那青年则以戏谑的口吻回应，把自己比作一个拾荒者，只能点燃一堆篝火。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, every man knows how to entertain with mirth. The tailor suggested that his lord might enjoy staying for the day instead of visiting friends, as he still appeared unwell and might encounter meddlesome talkers or busybodies who would give him a headache while he was weak from illness.
paragraphs.zh: 确实，每个人都知道如何用欢笑来消遣。裁缝建议他的主人不妨留在这里过一天，而不是去拜访朋友，因为他还显得不太舒服，可能会遇到爱管闲事的人，他们在自己身体虚弱的时候说三道四，可能会给自己添麻烦。

paragraphs.en: I said to him, "You have not failed in giving me your good advice," and despite my anger, I laughed. "Perhaps some other time, with God's will. Finish your business and go in peace, enjoy yourself with your friends."
paragraphs.zh: 我对他说：“你没有辜负我的期望，给了我很好的建议。”尽管心中仍有怒气，我还是笑了起来。“或许将来有机会吧，愿上帝保佑。你赶紧忙完自己的事，平安离去，和朋友们好好享受一番吧。”

paragraphs.en: He replied, "My lord, I only wish you would join us. There is no meddlesome or garrulous man among them. Since reaching manhood, I have never tolerated such company.
paragraphs.zh: 他回答说：“我的 Lord，我只希望您能加入我们。他们中没有爱管闲事或好说闲话的人。自成年后，我就从未忍受过这样的同伴。”

paragraphs.en: Spend some time with them, and you will forget all others."
paragraphs.zh: 与他们相处一段时间，你就会忘了其他人。

paragraphs.en: I said, "May God grant you joy. I must visit my friends today." The barber insisted, "If it were not today, let me take what you gave for your guests and return to you later."
paragraphs.zh: 我说：“愿上帝赐你快乐。我今天要去拜访朋友。”理发师坚持道：“如果不是今天，让我先收下你给客人的钱，等晚些时候再还给你。”

paragraphs.en: I replied, "Go in peace; I will see you with mine this day."
paragraphs.zh: 我回答说：“你去吧，今天我会向我的主为你祈祷。”

paragraphs.en: The barber protested, "My lord, I cannot leave you alone." I said, "I am going to a private party where you won't be welcome. You are the one who brings color to such places, but if it's just a woman, I need you less."
paragraphs.zh: 理发师抗议道：“我的老爷，我不能让您一个人留下。”我说：“我要去一个私人聚会，您不会被欢迎的。你才是能让这些地方生色的人，但如果只是女人在场，我就更不需要你了。”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until I tell you what comes next!"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫札德沉默不语。丁纳扎德remarked道：“这真是个奇怪而引人入胜的故事！”沙赫札德回答说：“你得等着听接下来的精彩部分了！”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began: "O happy King, the tailor told the king of China that the young man said to his guests..."
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙海拉罕开口说道：“幸福的国王啊，裁缝告诉中国的国王，那个来自巴格达的年轻男子对他的客人说……”

paragraphs.en: The barber said he was the best man for my plan, as no one would see me entering the place in Baghdad on such a day, given the powerful police chief. I retorted angrily, calling him an old fool who should be ashamed to speak so. He insisted that his help was necessary and that I shouldn't hide my plans from him.
paragraphs.zh: 理发师说他是我计划的最佳人选，因为考虑到那个强大的警察局长在场，没有人会注意到我那天进入巴格达的那个地方。我愤怒地反驳他，称他是个老糊涂，不该如此说话。但他坚持认为他的帮助必不可少，并且我不应该瞒着他。

paragraphs.en: Afraid of being exposed, I remained silent as he finished shaving my head. By noon, the first two prayer calls had ended, and it was time for the third. I told him to take food and drink to his friends while I waited for his return.
paragraphs.zh: 害怕被揭穿，我默不作声地让他剃完了我的头。中午时分，前两遍祷告已经结束，第三遍祷告开始了。我嘱咐他去给朋友们带些食物和饮料，自己则留在原地等待他的归来。

paragraphs.en: Despite my attempts to persuade him otherwise, he refused to leave, warning that I might fall into a trap.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管我一再试图说服他，他还是坚持不离开，并警告我说我可能会落入陷阱。

paragraphs.en: I agreed reluctantly, telling him not to be late. He took all the items—food, drink, roast lamb, and perfume—and left. However, instead of delivering them as instructed, he sent everything back with a porter and hid in an alley.
paragraphs.zh: 我勉强答应了他，叮嘱他不要迟到。他把所有东西——食物、饮料、烤羊肉和香水——都拿走了。然而，他并没有按指示送去，而是把一切退回给一名搬运工，并躲在了一条小巷里。

paragraphs.en: Upon hearing the call for prayer, I quickly dressed and headed to the house where I had seen the lady. The old woman was waiting at the door when I entered. Ascending to her daughter's room, I found the master returning from the mosque, closing the door behind him.
paragraphs.zh: 听到唤祷声，我迅速穿好衣服，赶往之前见到那位女士的那户人家。老妇人已在门口等候。我上楼来到她女儿的房间，只见房门刚被主人从清真寺关闭。

paragraphs.en: From my window, I saw the barber outside, who seemed to have followed me. Realizing he knew my whereabouts, I felt a wave of unease.
paragraphs.zh: 从我的窗子里，我看见那个理发师在外头似乎跟踪了上来。意识到他知道自己在哪里，我不由得感到一阵不安。

paragraphs.en: Just then, a maid was beaten by the master for an offense, causing her to scream. A slave tried to intervene but was also beaten and began screaming. The barber mistook this for me being punished and started tearing his clothes, throwing dust on himself, and crying out for help.
paragraphs.zh: 就在这时，女仆因犯错被主人打了一顿，痛得尖叫起来。一个奴隶试图干预也被打了，开始跟着尖叫。理发师误以为我在受罚，顿时扯开衣服，扬起尘土，大声呼救。

paragraphs.en: People gathered around him as he shouted that my master was being murdered in the judge's house.
paragraphs.zh: 人们围了上来，他喊道我的主人正在法官府中遭到谋杀。

paragraphs.en: He ran towards my house, followed by a crowd, including my family and servants who arrived in disarray, shouting "Alas for our master!" with the barber leading them, torn clothes flapping wildly.
paragraphs.zh: 他跑向我家，后面跟着一大群人，包括乱糟糟赶到的家人和仆从，喊着“我们的主人啊，真可惜！”理发师领头，破衣烂衫在风中飘动。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until I tell you more if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德沉默了。丁纳札德说道：“姐姐，这故事真引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答道：“只有国王饶恕我，我才能告诉你更多。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began: O happy King, the tailor recounted to you that the young man addressed his guests as follows...
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉扎德说道：幸福的国王啊，裁缝讲述道，那个年轻人对他的客人是这样说道……

paragraphs.en: The relatives cried out, "Alas for our murdered one," as a large crowd gathered. The judge heard the commotion and sent a servant to investigate. Upon returning, the servant reported that over ten thousand people were outside, crying and pointing at their house.
paragraphs.zh: 亲戚们悲痛地喊道：“啊，我们的死者！”随着人群迅速聚集。法官听到喧闹声，派了一个仆人去调查。仆人回来后报告说，外面聚集了上千人，他们一边哭泣一边指着那座房子。

paragraphs.en: Concerned, the judge opened the door and saw the crowd. He asked, "What is the matter?" They replied, "You cursed man, you have killed our master."
paragraphs.zh: 法官见状担忧地开了门，看到一群人围在那里，问道：“出了什么事？”众人回答说：“你这个该死的家伙，你杀了我们的主人。”

paragraphs.en: The judge responded, "Why would I kill him? My house is open to you." The barber interjected, saying he had heard his master screaming inside after being beaten with a rod.
paragraphs.zh: 法官回答：“我为什么要杀他？我家门永远向你敞开。”理发师插话说，他曾听到主人在被打得满身是伤后发出撕心裂肺的喊叫。

paragraphs.en: The barber continued, "Your daughter loves him and vice versa. When you found out, you ordered your servants to beat him. Only the caliph can judge us, or I will bring him out myself and shame you."
paragraphs.zh: 理发师接着说：“你的女儿爱着他，他也同样爱着她。你得知后下令让仆人将他打了一顿。只有哈里发才有权评判我们，否则我亲自把他带出来羞辱你。”

paragraphs.en: Blushing and tongue-tied, the judge muttered, "If what you say is true, come in and fetch him." The barber pushed forward and entered the house.
paragraphs.zh: 法官脸红而结巴，低声说道：“如果你说的属实，就进去把他带出来。”理发师推门先进了屋。

paragraphs.en: When the barber entered, I found no way to escape or hide except behind a large chest in the room. I hid inside, held my breath, and waited. The barber searched but only saw me in the chest.
paragraphs.zh: 当理发师进来时，我别无选择，只能躲到房间角落的一个大木箱后面。我藏了进去，屏住呼吸，等待着。理发师四处搜寻了一番，却只在箱子里面发现了我的踪迹。

paragraphs.en: He placed it on his head and left hurriedly. Panicked, I opened the chest, broke my leg, and fled through Baghdad's alleys as the barber chased after me.
paragraphs.zh: 他把东西戴在头上匆匆离开。我慌忙打开箱子，假装摔断了腿，在巴格达的巷子里狼狈逃窜，理发师紧随其后。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused, and Dinarzad said, "What a fascinating tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night to hear more."
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉扎德停了下来，丁兹扎德说道：“真是个引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉扎德回答道：“等到明天晚上你就会听到更多了。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard that the tailor told the king of China about the young man's words. He said he had run from his pursuers, who would have killed him and deprived him of his benefactor and family. But God had saved him.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说裁缝把那个年轻人的话告诉了中国的国王。他说自己曾逃亡，那些人本会杀了他，并剥夺了他的恩人和家人。但上帝救了他。

paragraphs.en: The barber asked where the young man wanted to go now, emphasizing how only he could save him. He warned that such foolishness nearly destroyed him but forgave the rash decision.
paragraphs.zh: 理发师问那年轻人现在想去哪里，强调只有他才能救下年轻人。他警告说这种愚蠢的行为差点要了他的命，但还是原谅了他鲁莽的决定。

paragraphs.en: The young man continued his story, explaining his escape and the barber's relentless pursuit.
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人继续讲述他的故事，解释了他如何逃脱以及理发师坚持不懈的追捕。

paragraphs.en: The barber continued his pursuit through Baghdad's streets until the young man lost patience and sought refuge in a caravansary. There, he made a will, dividing his wealth among his family and appointing a guardian to oversee them. He then left for this city, settling here after receiving an invitation.
paragraphs.zh: 理发师在巴格达的街道上继续追赶那个年轻人，直到年轻人终于失去了耐心，在一家客店避难。在那里，他立下了遗嘱，将财产分配给家人，并指定了一位监护人来照顾他们。随后，他接受了邀请，来到了这座城市，并在这里安顿下来。

paragraphs.en: Upon arrival, the young man encountered the barber again, seated in honor. This encounter ruined any chance of enjoyment; the barber had caused him to break his leg, abandon his home, and go into exile. Now, he found himself face-to-face with the very person who brought all this upon him.
paragraphs.zh: 一到那里，年轻人又遇到了那位坐在显要位置的理发师。这次相遇彻底破坏了他任何享受的机会；正是理发师让他摔断了腿，不得不放弃家园，流亡海外。如今，他与当初给他带来这一切不幸的人面对面站着。

paragraphs.en: The group was amazed by the young man's tale and questioned the barber about it. The barber defended himself, claiming he acted out of wisdom and humanity, saving the young man from a worse fate. He boasted that among his six brothers, he was the least meddlesome and talkative, and proceeded to recount an incident to prove his point.
paragraphs.zh: 众人对年轻人的故事感到惊讶，便询问理发师此事的详情。理发师为自己辩护，声称自己出于智慧和仁慈之心，救了年轻人一命，避免他陷入更糟的境地。他得意地说，在自己的六个兄弟中，自己是最不善管闲事、也不爱多嘴多舌的一个，并且举了一个例子来证明这一点。

paragraphs.en: In the Middle East, barbers often serve as surgeons and dentists today. Astrologers once used a tool to determine celestial positions. These duties reflect the diverse skills expected of professionals in that region.
paragraphs.zh: 在中东，理发师如今常常兼任外科医生和牙医。占星家曾使用某种工具来推算天体位置。这些职责反映了该地区专业人员所应具备的多样技能。
